judgementCalls.question: Does 'annihilate is permanently unavailable for a registered stablecoin' satisfy the C4 Medium clause 'the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted', and is the compound case (sole registered stable, no replacement) realistic or hypothetical?
judgementCalls.verdict: LOW - HELD, but this is the run's closest call and it is REFERRED FOR SECOND OPINION
judgementCalls.reasoning: The Medium clause is engaged on its face and I am not pretending otherwise: annihilate is the ONLY thing Antimatter does, so bricking a pair is a total functional outage for every holder whose stablecoin that is, and trigger T3 (an honest, correctly-registered token whose decimals() is not view-callable) is PROVEN by PoC and involves no misbehaviour by anyone - it is purely this delta's own new strictness. Three things hold it at Low, and the first is the decisive one. (1) NOTHING IS CONSUMED AND NOTHING IS LOST. The revert is inside toStableAmount, reached at :230, strictly BEFORE the _burn at :239 and before any transfer. No antimatter is burned, no stablecoin is pulled, no phUSD is minted. The entitlement is DELAYED, not destroyed; C4 Medium's other limb ('leak value') is therefore not engaged at all, and only the availability limb is in play. (2) THE OUTAGE IS ROUTABLE-AROUND AND SINGLE-TRANSACTION RECOVERABLE. `stable` is a free caller-supplied parameter, so any holder with a second registered stablecoin simply pairs against it; and the owner closes the outage by registering one working alternative. Under Law 3 the owner is trusted and responsive - assuming an owner who never acts, in order to convert a recoverable outage into a permanent one, is exactly the kind of assumption C4 calls hand-wavy. (3) THE COMPOUND CASE IS NOT ESTABLISHED AT HEAD. It needs sole-registered-stable AND that token exhibiting T1/T2/T3 AND no owner response. Antimatter is not wired into staging (established in run-01) and no deployment evidence in this run fixes the registered-stablecoin set at one, so the conjunction is asserted, not observed - and a conjunction of unobserved terms is the definition of a hypothetical. Additionally, for trigger T1 specifically (a registered proxy stablecoin dropping decimals() post-registration) the MARGINAL risk is near zero: any token you registered can already brick annihilate unilaterally by reverting transferFrom, pausing, or blacklisting Antimatter, so T1 adds no capability an adversarial token did not already have. What survives, and is genuinely new and genuinely the protocol's own fault, is T2/T3 - and both of those are registration-time properties that the FIRST annihilate against that token exposes. That makes them an operational/registration-checklist hazard, which is Low, aggravated by the real asymmetry the econ scanner found: PhusdStableMinter.mint keeps working for the same token (the minter reads only its own config.decimals), so a mint-path smoke test shows the protocol healthy while the antimatter path is dead. I record that asymmetry as the reason this sits at the TOP of Low rather than the bottom, and as the reason a second opinion is warranted rather than assumed unnecessary.
escalateToMediumIf: Deployment evidence shows exactly ONE stablecoin registered on the minter Antimatter points at, at any time antimatter is being distributed as a staking reward. That single fact converts 'routable-around' into 'total outage' and I would move this to Medium on it alone.
Any registered stablecoin is observed to exhibit T1/T2/T3 on a live network.
A future change moves the toStableAmount call AFTER the burn, or introduces any path where the revert can strand consumed assets.

judgementCalls.question: Same Medium clause, harder trigger: does a registered token able to push toStableAmount past the block gas limit impact protocol availability enough for Medium?
judgementCalls.reasoning: Measured and real (16,782 gas at 32 bytes; 1,815,823 at 640KB; 158,677,386 at 6.4MB; OOG under a 30M cap at 64MB) and the DoS reaches both annihilate for the pair and the public toStableAmount quote helper. It stays Low on the MARGINAL-CAPABILITY test: the only actor who can pull this trigger is the registered stablecoin itself, and that actor already holds unconditional, cheaper power to brick annihilate for its own pair by reverting transferFrom, pausing, or blacklisting Antimatter. This defect therefore grants a hostile-or-broken registered token no capability it lacked, which is what separates it from L-05 - L-05 has a trigger (T3) reachable by an HONEST token, this one does not. An honest token does not answer decimals() with kilobytes. Nor is it profitable to anyone: fails closed, no burn (the revert/OOG precedes :239), no theft, no griefing of a third party by an unprivileged attacker (registration is owner-gated and the StablecoinNotRegistered guard at :285 correctly runs FIRST, so no caller can aim toStableAmount at an address of their choosing). What keeps it reportable rather than suppressed is the Law-3 footgun half the sanitizer already ruled on and I adopt: it is registration-GATED, not owner-CAUSED, the realistic path is a token changing implementation AFTER registration - outside the owner's control - and no competent owner expects registering a token to hand that token a block-gas-limit lever over a public view function. Filed as a robustness/defence-in-depth Low with a cheap, complete fix.

judgementCalls.question: Does a guard whose NAME and COMMENT claim protection it does not provide rise above QA?
judgementCalls.verdict: QA - HELD, with a mandatory false-closure attestation attached
judgementCalls.reasoning: On its own the check causes NOTHING: it is strictly stricter than the post-condition it replaced, so every state it newly rejects is a state in which the caller was short-changed. Zero asset impact, zero availability impact - C4 QA ('issues with comments' / 'function incorrect as to spec') is the honest band and inflating it would be overstatement. The reason it is not noise is downstream and is a Law-1 hazard rather than a severity: the comment at :232-233 ('a short mint cannot pass unnoticed') and the error name PhUSDAmountMismatch read as a slippage guard, and a future triager could reasonably conclude ledger F-01 (3aac91383dcb6060, 'no minimum-output guard on an already-irreversible burn') has been closed by it. It has not been. Both sides of the equality are the SAME pure view (minter.calculateMintAmount) called with the SAME arguments in the SAME transaction against the SAME config storage, so the two agree by construction on 100% of the honest path; an owner who lowers exchangeRate mid-flight settles a pending annihilate at the new rate (150 phUSD instead of 200, burn already irreversible) and the check passes precisely BECAUSE it re-quotes at the new rate. The standing rule that in-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority and RAISES severity when falsely exhaustive is applied here in its correct form: it stops this from being culled as a nitpick, but it does not manufacture asset impact where there is none. The protection is therefore the routing (channel false-closure-watch, WATCH-02-02 tripwire, and the closureBlock recorded on this entry), not the label.

judgementCalls.question: What is the honest band for a Law-2 provenance deviation whose CODE is safe - indeed is the audit's own recommended mitigation?
judgementCalls.verdict: LOW - HELD (the deduplicator's roll-up to qa is DECLINED; the story-faithfulness agent's Low stands)
judgementCalls.reasoning: Law 2 is a report-ROUTING law before it is a severity law: this is tagged faithfulness=true and goes to spec-conformance as F-04 at honest severity, never into the QA/gas bundle, and that routing is not negotiable regardless of band. On the band itself: the code is safe, tested, strictly stricter than what it replaced, and implements run-01 F-01's own recommended mitigation almost verbatim, so there is no security escalation and Medium is not remotely in play. But qa is too low, for a specific and checkable reason rather than a stylistic one: an UNREVIEWED, UNTAGGED behavioural change to annihilate's settlement post-condition landed in the same delta as the fixes for the project's only open High (H-01 <- story-001) and its open Medium (M-01 <- story-002), and story-001 named the PhUSDNotReceived assertion in an explicit do-not-touch list with the words 'This story is a signature and authorisation change, not a rewrite of the settlement logic.' The traceability of the fix-wave does not extend to it, and because no story records the decision there are NO acceptance criteria against which a future regression of this post-condition could be graded. That is a durable, material gap in the record of the one function every open finding passes through - Low, not a comment nit. Note also the tension this exposes and does not resolve: the same commit that Q-05 shows OVER-CLAIMS its coverage is the commit that has NO story authorising it. Both facts point at the same missing review.

judgementCalls.question: Is single-step Ownable reportable at all, and what is it NOT?
judgementCalls.verdict: QA - HELD, filed as centralization/governance (C-03), with an explicit provenance statement
judgementCalls.reasoning: C4 puts governance/admin-privilege matters in QA by definition, and both possible escalations fail. The footgun half is admitted but its consequence is OBVIOUS - a competent owner is not surprised that mistyping an address in transferOwnership hands over the contract - so it fails the Law-3 surprise test and is trusted-owner territory, not a submission-grade hazard. The automated-tool half applies as a SEVERITY CEILING ONLY, never as a suppression: C4 discounts common tool findings without a demonstrated H/M path, which caps it at QA, but Law 1 forbids withholding it from the scan on that basis - cull it at /ledger triage if unwanted, not here. PROVENANCE, stated explicitly as instructed and repeated on the finding itself: this is NOT a regression and was NOT introduced by the 0bb82d8..c91bc1a delta. Antimatter has inherited single-step Ownable since before the baseline. It is a run-01 COVERAGE GAP surfaced now only because 4naly3er was repaired between runs, and any downstream stage that files it as a regression or attributes it to this delta is wrong. Its practical weight is as a multiplier on ledger C-02 (Antimatter has no kill switch of its own): every incident lever this protocol has runs through an owner key whose transfer has no undo.

findings.label: L-04
findings.title: The new decimals() staticcall copies unbounded return data and forwards all remaining gas, so a registered token can make toStableAmount - and therefore every annihilation of that pair - cost more gas than a block allows
findings.severityAgreementNote: AGREES with the incoming Low, but re-derived independently rather than inherited: Medium was tested explicitly on the availability clause and declined on the marginal-capability test recorded in judgementCalls.
findings.c4Criterion: QA/Low - 'state handling' / robustness. It does not meet Medium because the availability impact it causes can already be caused more cheaply and unconditionally by the only actor able to cause it at all, so no protocol capability is newly lost; and it does not meet High because nothing is stolen or destroyed (the revert precedes the burn at :239).

classification.assetImpact: NONE - no theft, no burn, no stranded value. The failure is entirely a denial of service: annihilate() is unusable for the affected pair (it routes through toStableAmount at :230) and the public toStableAmount quote helper is unusable for off-chain callers. Antimatter is not consumed on this path, so holders keep their tokens and their entitlement.
attackPath: 1. Owner registers stablecoin S. The StablecoinNotRegistered guard at :285 runs FIRST, so no caller can aim toStableAmount at an address of their own choosing - registration is the only way in.
2. S's implementation is subsequently changed (upgradeable proxy) so that decimals() returns a very large ABI blob, or simply burns gas.

3. Any call to toStableAmount(S, x) executes `(bool ok, bytes memory data) = stable.staticcall(...)` at :292, which allocates and RETURNDATACOPYs the ENTIRE return buffer before `data.length != 32` is evaluated at :293. Memory expansion is quadratic, so the caller pays for the callee's choice. All remaining gas is forwarded, so a gas-burning decimals() reaches the same outcome via the 63/64 rule.
4. Measured: 16,782 gas for a 32-byte answer; 1,815,823 gas at 640KB; 158,677,386 gas at 6.4MB; out-of-gas under a 30,000,000 gas cap at 64MB.
5. annihilate(S, ...) and eth_call quoting for S are both dead for as long as S behaves that way.
classification.likelihood: LOW. Requires the registered token itself to be hostile or catastrophically broken - no honest token answers decimals() with kilobytes, and no unprivileged third party can introduce such a token. Crucially, a token capable of this ALREADY holds cheaper unilateral power to brick annihilate for its own pair (revert transferFrom, pause, blacklist Antimatter), so the marginal likelihood-weighted risk this adds is close to zero.
classification.assumptions: A token that has been owner-registered as a supported stablecoin later returns an unbounded return buffer from decimals(), or burns the gas forwarded to it.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner registration of the token (a prerequisite, not the cause), plus a post-registration change in the token's implementation - an upgradeable proxy is the realistic vehicle. Outside the owner's control.

findings.law3Verdict: FOOTGUN, IN SCOPE. Adopted from the sanitizer and re-tested here: registration-GATED, not owner-CAUSED. The trigger is a third party's post-registration implementation change, and a competent, non-malicious owner would be SURPRISED that registering a token hands that token a block-gas-limit lever over a public view function on the annihilation path. Surprise => footgun => reported. NOT classified on any 'malicious owner' basis.
findings.justification: Held at LOW. The measurement is unambiguous and the DoS is real, but severity must reflect what is NEWLY at risk, and the answer is almost nothing: the exclusive trigger-holder is the registered token, and that token can already deny annihilation for its own pair at will and for less gas. That is the whole difference between this finding and L-05, which has an honest-token trigger and therefore sits above it. Not raised to Medium: no capability is newly granted, nothing is consumed, no unprivileged attacker participates, and no value leaks - all four of Medium's routes are shut. Not suppressed as 'weird ERC20' or as a reckless admin mistake either: the C4 known-invalid list covers admin RECKLESSNESS, and registering a stablecoin is the intended operation, while the hostile behaviour appears afterwards. The defect worth fixing is a one-line discipline failure - read exactly one word, bound the gas - and its fix costs nothing, which is itself an argument for reporting it rather than absorbing it. This is defence-in-depth, correctly labelled as such.
findings.recommendation: Read exactly one word and ignore the rest: an assembly staticcall with a 32-byte output buffer plus an explicit `returndatasize() == 32` check, and/or cap the forwarded gas (`{gas: 30000}` is ample for any real decimals()). The stated reason at :289-291 for preferring a raw staticcall over try/catch (an uncatchable uint8 decode of a >255 value) remains valid and is entirely unaffected by this change.

findings.label: L-05
findings.title: Annihilation now hard-depends on every registered stablecoin answering decimals() through a static call; a token that cannot, or stops, strands that pair's reward entitlement while the minter's own path keeps working
findings.severityAgreementNote: AGREES with the incoming Low as a final band, but this was the run's closest call and it is NOT a quiet agreement: Medium was argued in full on the C4 availability clause, three specific deflators carried the day, and the finding is REFERRED to severity-auditor with a concrete escalation trigger. If the deciding evidence lands the other way this becomes a Medium.
findings.c4Criterion: QA/Low - state handling / operational-configuration hazard. The C4 Medium clause 'the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted' IS engaged on its face and was declined on likelihood and recoverability, not on mechanism: nothing is consumed (the revert at :293/:295 precedes _burn at :239), `stable` is a free parameter so holders route around it whenever a second stablecoin is registered, and one owner transaction restores service. The value-leak limb of Medium is not engaged at all.

classification.assetImpact: NO LOSS, DELAYED REALISATION. Antimatter is inert held alone; its entire value is the phUSD that annihilation emits. While the condition persists, that already-distributed reward entitlement cannot be realised against the affected stablecoin. But the revert happens in toStableAmount (reached from :230), strictly BEFORE _burn at :239 and before any transfer, so no antimatter is burned, no stablecoin is pulled, no phUSD is minted, and nothing is stranded on-chain. A holder who chooses to exit during the outage does so at whatever discount the market applies to a temporarily unredeemable claim - that is a market consequence of an outage, not a protocol loss, and it is not counted as value leak here.
attackPath: NO ATTACKER IS REQUIRED - this is a liveness/configuration hazard, and it is classified as one. Three enumerated triggers:
T1: a registered upgradeable stablecoin ships an implementation where decimals() reverts or is dropped, while transfer/transferFrom keep working.

T2: the owner registers an old-style token that never had decimals() at all - annihilate never works for it from day one, silently, because the minter supplied the decimals at registration and nothing else on the mint path asks the token.

T3 (PROVEN, and the one that matters): an HONEST, correctly-registered token whose decimals() is not view - it increments a counter, lazily caches, or emits - is rejected by STATICCALL with ok == false and reverts DecimalsUnavailable, even though its registration is correct and its answer would have matched.

Consequence in all three: every annihilate(S, ...) reverts at :293, while PhusdStableMinter.mint(S, ...) continues to work perfectly (the minter reads only its own config.decimals at minter:254 and never queries the token's metadata). Mint-path monitoring shows the protocol healthy; only antimatter holders see the outage.
Recovery: the owner registers a working alternative stablecoin, or holders pair against any other already-registered one.
classification.likelihood: LOW-TO-MODERATE for the outage; LOW for the outage becoming PERMANENT. T3 is proven reachable and requires no misbehaviour by anyone, but no real stablecoin an owner would register implements decimals() as non-view, and T2/T3 are registration-time properties that the very first annihilate against that token exposes. T1 requires a real stablecoin to drop decimals() post-upgrade, which would break most of DeFi and is correspondingly improbable - and for T1 the marginal risk is small anyway, since such a token could already brick annihilate by reverting transferFrom. Permanence additionally requires an owner who never responds, which Law 3's trusted, non-malicious owner does not license as an assumption.
classification.assumptions: STATED IN FULL. (a) A registered stablecoin's decimals() is unavailable through a static call - by upgrade (T1), by absence (T2), or by being non-view (T3). (b) FOR THE SEVERE CASE ONLY: that stablecoin is the sole registered one, or the affected holders hold only that one. (c) FOR PERMANENCE ONLY: the owner does not promptly register an alternative. Assumptions (b) and (c) are NOT established at c91bc1a - Antimatter is not wired into staging and no deployment evidence in this run fixes the registered set at one - which is precisely why the compound case is treated as hypothetical and the finding is held at Low.
classification.externalRequirements: A third-party token's metadata behaviour, which the protocol does not control, plus (for the severe case) a single-stablecoin configuration and an unresponsive owner.

findings.law3Verdict: FOOTGUN, IN SCOPE. Adopted from the sanitizer and independently upheld: the owner would reasonably assume the minter's own registered `decimals` field is the authority - that is why the minter carries the field - and would be surprised both that annihilation additionally requires the token to self-report, and that the resulting failure is INVISIBLE on the minter path while fatal on the antimatter path. T3 is not an owner error at all. NOT classified on any 'malicious owner' basis; the owner cannot usefully cause this deliberately and third-party token behaviour is what changes.
findings.justification: Held at LOW after the Medium case was argued at full strength, which is recorded in judgementCalls rather than summarised away. The three deflators are: nothing is consumed (fail-closed before the burn, so this is delay and not loss, and the value-leak limb of Medium never engages); the outage is routable-around by the caller because `stable` is a free parameter; and it is recoverable by the owner in a single registration transaction, which under Law 3's trusted, responsive owner is the expected course. The compound case that would make this a genuine protocol-wide outage - sole registered stablecoin, no replacement - is a conjunction of terms none of which is observed at HEAD, and an unobserved conjunction is what C4 means by a hypothetical. What keeps it at the TOP of Low rather than the bottom is the asymmetry the econ scanner identified and I confirmed against PhusdStableMinter:254: the mint path keeps working for the same token, so the standard smoke test passes while the antimatter product is dead. That is a genuine detection gap, it is newly introduced by this delta (at 0bb82d8 toStableAmount made no call to `stable` at all), and it argues for the escalation trigger recorded below rather than for a comfortable closure now. I am deliberately NOT deflating this to keep the report tidy: it is flagged borderline, referred for a second opinion, and given an evidence-based route to Medium.
escalateToMediumIf: Exactly ONE stablecoin is registered on the minter Antimatter points at while antimatter is being distributed as a staking reward - this alone moves it to Medium.
Any registered stablecoin is observed exhibiting T1/T2/T3 on a live network.
Any future change moves the toStableAmount call after _burn, so a revert can strand consumed assets.
findings.recommendation: Preferred: treat an UNAVAILABLE decimals() as 'no independent confirmation available' and fall back to the minter's registered value, keeping the hard revert only for a decimals() that answers and DISAGREES - which is the actual misconfiguration ledger M-01 aimed at, and which INV6 confirms is closed in both directions. Alternative: perform the cross-check once at registration/acceptance time on Antimatter's side and cache it, so a later change in token behaviour cannot brick already-distributed rewards. If accepted as-is: document the operational requirement that at least two independently-implemented stablecoins are registered at all times, add 'decimals() must be view-callable' to the registration checklist, widen the DecimalsUnavailable NatSpec (which today says only 'does not report usable decimals at all') to say 'through a static call', and run a monitor that calls toStableAmount(S, 1e18) per registered S - the mint path cannot detect this failure.

notes.relatedTo: L-04 (same call site, same delta). DO NOT COLLAPSE: L-04 needs a hostile or broken token and is defence-in-depth; L-05 is reachable by an honest token and is an operational hazard. Their fixes are different - bounding the copy does not make an unavailable decimals() available.
notes.interactionWithM01: The cross-check this finding critiques is the fix for ledger M-01 (a1c81428a47ad295, fix-pending) and INV6 confirms it CLOSES M-01's exploit path in both directions. This finding is the cost of that fix, not an argument to revert it - hence the recommendation preserves the disagreement revert and softens only the unavailable case.
notes.boundaryNote: Per MR-02-P3, M-01's closure is BOUNDARY-SCOPED - correct for Antimatter, silent for PhusdStableMinter's own permissionless mint. That warning is carried by MR-02-P3 and is not restated as a finding here.

findings.label: Q-05
findings.title: The new exact-equality quote check is a tautology on any honest minter, yet its comment and error name present it as protection against being short-changed - which risks a future reader believing ledger F-01 has been fixed when it has not
findings.severityAgreementNote: AGREES with the incoming QA. Low was tested and declined: the check causes no asset or availability impact of its own. The standing rule that falsely-exhaustive in-source docs RAISE severity is applied to stop this being culled as a nitpick, not to manufacture impact - the real protection is the false-closure block recorded on this entry.
findings.c4Criterion: QA/Low - 'function incorrect as to spec, issues with comments'. Squarely the comment/spec limb. It does not reach Medium: the new post-condition is strictly STRICTER than the one it replaced, so it removes no capability, impairs no availability, and leaks no value.
findings.faithfulnessNote: Deliberately NOT tagged faithfulness. This is a defect in what the code's own comment claims, not a deviation from a story - no story speaks to this post-condition at all, which is exactly what F-04 reports. Keeping them separate keeps both visible.

classification.assetImpact: NONE from the check itself. The impact it FAILS to prevent is ledger F-01's, unchanged: an owner who lowers exchangeRate while an annihilate is in flight settles that caller at the new rate - 100 AM burned, 100 USDC pulled, 150 phUSD delivered instead of 200 - with the burn already irreversible and no caller-supplied minimum anywhere.
attackPath: 1. `expectedForStable = minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount)` at :234.
2. PhusdStableMinter.mint computes its own phUSDAmount at PhusdStableMinter.sol:212 by calling the SAME public view with IDENTICAL arguments in the SAME transaction against the same config storage.

3. Neither exchangeRate nor decimals can change between :234 and :251 - both are onlyOwner setters and no path reaches them mid-call - so the two sides agree BY CONSTRUCTION and the check at :257 is a no-op on 100% of the honest path.
4. Owner calls minter.updateExchangeRate(usdc, 0.5e18) while Alice's annihilate(usdc, alice, 100e18) is pending. Alice lands at the new rate and receives 150 phUSD instead of 200.
5. expectedForStable (50e18) EQUALS mintedForStable (50e18) - because the check re-quotes at the NEW rate too - so PhUSDAmountMismatch does not fire and the code reports success.

6. A reader of the comment at :232-233 ('Measuring against its own quote, rather than merely against zero, means a short mint cannot pass unnoticed') and of the error name PhUSDAmountMismatch would reasonably believe otherwise.
classification.likelihood: The tautology is CERTAIN - it holds on every successful call. The mis-settlement it does not catch has the likelihood already recorded against ledger F-01 and is not re-counted here.
classification.assumptions: The minter behaves as written. The check does retain narrow genuine value against a FUTURE minter whose mint() diverges from its own quote, and against Antimatter's phUSD balance moving between the :244 snapshot and the :256 read - the finding is the overstated framing, not the check's presence.
classification.externalRequirements: None for the tautology. An owner rate change mid-flight for the uncaught mis-settlement.

findings.justification: QA is the honest band and inflating it would be overstatement, which the pipeline rejects. But this finding's value is not its band - it is a TRIPWIRE, and it must survive triage as one. The new code now LOOKS like the guard ledger F-01 asked for without being it, and that is strictly worse for a future reader than the guard's plain absence was: a triager comparing F-01's recommendation ('assert mintedForStable against calculateMintAmount') against :234/:257 would find an apparent match and close a live finding. F-01 (3aac91383dcb6060) is 'no minimum-output guard on an already-irreversible burn', and no minimum-output guard exists at c91bc1a - there is no caller-supplied minimum parameter anywhere in annihilate. Note the interaction with F-04: the same untagged commit that OVER-CLAIMS its coverage here is the commit that no story authorises. Both point at the same missing review.

falseClosureBlock.attestationRequiredBeforeClosingF01: F-01 may be marked fixed ONLY on evidence of a CALLER-SUPPLIED minimum-output parameter (e.g. `uint256 minPhUSDOut` checked as `amount + mintedForStable >= minPhUSDOut` before :260). The :234/:257 exact-equality pair does NOT satisfy this and must never be cited as satisfying it: both sides re-quote from the same view in the same transaction, so the check tracks an owner rate change instead of resisting it.

findings.recommendation: Either (i) reword :232-233 to state what the check actually covers - 'the minter's mint() must agree with its own calculateMintAmount(); this is NOT a slippage guard' - and rename the error accordingly; or (ii) close F-01 properly by adding a `uint256 minPhUSDOut` parameter to annihilate and checking `amount + mintedForStable >= minPhUSDOut` before :260. Option (ii) subsumes (i) and is preferred.

evidence.poc: reasoning-only, and complete: the tautology is proven by reading PhusdStableMinter.sol:212 against Antimatter.sol:234 - same pure view, same arguments, same transaction, same storage.

findings.label: F-04
findings.title: An untagged commit rewrites the annihilation settlement post-condition on top of a two-story fix-wave: no story authorises it, and story-001 explicitly forbade touching that logic
findings.severityAgreementNote: AGREES with the story-faithfulness agent's filed Low and DECLINES the deduplicator's roll-up to qa. Stated as a disagreement because it is one: the deviation concerns the settlement post-condition of the single function every open finding passes through, and it left no acceptance criteria behind - that is more than a comment nit.
findings.c4Criterion: QA/Low - 'function incorrect as to spec'. Reported at Low and ROUTED to the spec-conformance report as a Law-2 deviation, never into the QA/gas bundle (CRITICAL RULE 6). No security escalation: the code change is safe, so neither High nor Medium is engaged.
findings.storyTag: none (untagged commit c91bc1a, subject 'more precise mint requirement')
findings.specText: story-001, Required deltas #5: 'Everything else - the check order, the burn-before-interactions ordering, the balance snapshots, the forceApprove/reset pair, the StableNotDeposited and PhUSDNotReceived assertions, the split _phUSD.mint(recipient, amount) + safeTransfer(recipient, mintedForStable) delivery - stays exactly as it is. This story is a signature and authorisation change, not a rewrite of the settlement logic.'

classification.assetImpact: NONE. The new post-condition is strictly stricter than the one it replaces: every state the old check accepted and the new one rejects is a state in which the caller received less than, or differently from, the minter's own quote. Substantively the change implements run-01 F-01's own recommended mitigation almost verbatim and incidentally narrows ledger L-01's donation-attribution gap.
classification.likelihood: n/a - a provenance and traceability deviation, not an exploit path.

findings.actualBehavior: c91bc1a - untagged, landed after both story commits - adds a pre-loop quote at :231-232 (`expectedForStable = minter.calculateMintAmount(...)`; `if (expectedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();`) and replaces the post-hoc `if (mintedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();` with `if (mintedForStable != expectedForStable) revert PhUSDAmountMismatch(expectedForStable, mintedForStable);` at :248. A new error is declared and PhUSDNotReceived is REPURPOSED to mean 'the quote itself was zero', now raised BEFORE the burn instead of after it. 51 lines of new tests accompany it.
findings.deviation: Neither story sanctions a change to the phUSD settlement post-condition. Story-001 names the PhUSDNotReceived assertion in an explicit do-not-touch list and says the story is 'not a rewrite of the settlement logic'; story-002 is confined to toStableAmount. This is un-storied work riding on a two-story fix-wave, and the fix-wave's traceability (H-01 <- story-001, M-01 <- story-002) does not extend to it.
findings.justification: Low, routed to spec-conformance. Law 2 is a routing law before it is a severity law, and that routing is not negotiable at any band. On the band: the code is safe, tested, strictly stricter than what it replaced, and is the audit's own recommendation, so there is no security escalation and Medium is not in play. It is not QA either, for a checkable reason: an unreviewed, untagged behavioural change to annihilate's settlement post-condition landed in the SAME delta as the fixes for the project's only open High and its open Medium, in the one function every open finding passes through, and story-001 had explicitly placed that assertion out of bounds. Because nothing in the story tree records the decision, there are no acceptance criteria against which a future regression of this post-condition could be graded - the gap is durable and it is exactly what a story-faithfulness pass exists to make visible. Law 2 is GRADED here, not deferred: the story tree resolved this run and stories 001 and 002 were read in full. This is not a 'story unavailable' non-answer.
findings.recommendation: Write the story - or amend story-002 / add story-003 - recording this decision, its acceptance criteria and its failure-mode analysis, so the exact-equality post-condition has a documented intent to be graded against in future regressions. NO CODE CHANGE IS REQUIRED for this finding. When that story is written, address Q-05 in it: the comment at :232-233 claims coverage the check does not provide, and the story is the right place to decide whether the intent is the narrow check that exists or the slippage guard the comment describes.

evidence.verification: git show c91bc1a -- src/Antimatter.sol; git log --oneline 0bb82d8..c91bc1a shows c91bc1a is the only untagged commit in the delta.

findings.label: C-03
findings.title: Antimatter inherits single-step OpenZeppelin Ownable rather than Ownable2Step, so a mistyped transferOwnership permanently loses every owner power the protocol depends on
findings.severityAgreementNote: AGREES with the incoming QA. Filed under the C- (centralization/governance) series rather than Q- because that is what it is: an admin-privilege structure finding, matching how run-01 labelled C-01 and C-02.
findings.c4Criterion: QA/Low - 'Governance/Centralization risk including admin privileges'. This is the definitional case. It cannot reach Medium or High: no attacker participates, no asset moves, and the loss scenario is the owner's own uncoerced typo - which C4 lists as a known-invalid admin mistake and Law 3 treats as trusted-owner territory.
findings.regressionStatement: EXPLICITLY NOT A REGRESSION, AND NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS DELTA. Antimatter has inherited single-step Ownable since before the 0bb82d8 baseline; the 0bb82d8..c91bc1a delta did not touch the import at :8 or the inheritance at :22. This is a run-01 COVERAGE GAP - 4naly3er/Semgrep did not run in run-01 - surfaced now only because the tooling was repaired between runs. Any downstream stage that files it as a regression, or attributes it to c91bc1a, is wrong.

classification.assetImpact: No direct impact and no attacker. If ownership is transferred to an address that cannot act, every owner power the protocol depends on is lost irreversibly: setPhUSD, setPhUSDMinter, setApprovedMinter, stablecoin registration decisions and rescueERC20. Antimatter would be frozen in whatever configuration it held at that moment.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls transferOwnership(addr) with a mistyped, unowned, or non-signing address.
2. OpenZeppelin's single-step Ownable transfers immediately - there is no acceptOwnership step and no undo.
3. All owner-gated functions are permanently unreachable.
classification.likelihood: Low, and entirely self-inflicted. No external actor can trigger it and no market or timing condition is involved.
classification.assumptions: The owner mistypes or supplies an address that cannot sign.
classification.externalRequirements: None - which is also why it is not a security finding.

findings.law3Verdict: TRUSTED-OWNER TERRITORY for the ESCALATION, but still FILED at QA. The footgun half is admitted and its consequence is OBVIOUS - no competent owner is surprised that mistyping an address in transferOwnership hands over the contract - so it fails the Law-3 surprise test and does not qualify as a submission-grade operational hazard. That declines the escalation only; it does not license withholding the finding, which Law 1 forbids.
findings.justification: QA, and correctly so on two independent grounds that both cap rather than suppress. First, C4 places governance and admin-privilege matters in QA by definition. Second, this is a common automated-tool finding with no demonstrated H/M exploit path, which C4 discounts - but that applies AS A SEVERITY CEILING ONLY, never as a suppression: Law 1 says cull noise at /ledger triage, not by withholding it from the scan. Its practical weight is as a multiplier on ledger C-02 (Antimatter has no kill switch of its own): every incident lever this protocol has runs through an owner key whose transfer has no undo, and the open High H-01 is a one-transaction theft that Antimatter's own owner already has no proportionate lever to stop. Cheap to fix, so worth fixing; not worth more than QA.
findings.originNote: origin 'new' means NEW TO THE LEDGER (first time filed), not new to the code. See regressionStatement - the code predates the baseline.
findings.recommendation: Inherit Ownable2Step instead of Ownable so ownership transfer requires the incoming owner to call acceptOwnership. One-line change, no behavioural cost, and it composes with the incident-response runbook C-02 already asks for.

notes.relatedTo: C-02 (3a90280bed325637, no local pause authority) - a multiplier on it, not a duplicate of it.
